functions.purpose: CORE host->network packer (tdr_host2net). Walks the meta tree with an explicit stack of frames (stride 0x2f ints = 188 bytes/frame, in aiStack_1784[]), converting each host struct field to big-endian (network) byte order and writing it into the net buffer. Handles: primitive scalars (1/2/4/8-byte BE swap), fixed arrays, refer/count-driven arrays, unions, version-indicator emission, C strings (type 0x15) and wstrings (type 0x16, UTF16 via FUN_100108a0). This is the codec that emits every TLV/TDR network message the server sends and parses — protocol-critical.
functions.serverRelevance: authoritative infrastructure: server MUST use byte-identical packing (BE order, size prefixes, version indicator, bounds checks) for wire compatibility with the client. Not skill computation itself, but every skill/buff TLV packet flows through this.

max nesting depth = 0x20 (32) layers; iStack_17cc>0x1f -> 0x82010404 'too complex, more than 32 layers'
sizeinfo overflow check uses 64-bit limit table at DAT_11e11420(lo)/DAT_11e11424(hi) indexed by sizeinfoSize*8: if value exceeds limit -> 0x82010479
refer/array count read from entry+0x58 (size 0/2/4/8) at host offset entry+0x5c; validated 0 <= refer <= arrayCount(entry+0x24) else 0x82010403
BE swap 16-bit: (v<<8)|(v>>8); 32-bit: ((v&0xff0000|v>>0x10)>>8)|((v<<0x10|v&0xff00)<<8); 64-bit swaps both dwords and exchanges them

net-buffer overrun -> 0x82010402; string/wstring length errors -> 0x82010406
wstring byte length = FUN_100108a0(...)*2 + 2 (UTF16 + NUL); string length = strnlen+1

functions.purpose: Core anti-cheat / rate-limiter for skill-driven state transitions. Resolves the next-state definition object (FUN_10fb8160) from the 4-word state id and the current-state object (FUN_10fd05d0). Verifies the skill actually maps to a valid transition between current and next state (FUN_10fd4810). Then enforces a timing constraint: the elapsed time since last transition must not be shorter than the animation-defined limit multiplied by an 'FsmTolerance' factor. Logs detailed diagnostics when rejecting.
formulas: increments transition counter: *(param_1+0x74) += 1

FsmTolerance CVar read via FUN_100b62c0("FsmTolerance",""); default multiplier = _DAT_11cbf11c (float). If CVar present, multiplier = (float)(cvarInt + 100) / DAT_11de9a30 (DAT_11de9a30 almost certainly 100.0 => tolerance% -> factor)
limited = animLimitTime(local_c) * multiplier, where local_c = (float)auVar13 * param_4 (param_4 = duration/speed input)
elapsed cached = FUN_11484e10(vtbl+0x294(param_1+0x28,+0x40,+0x58)) then * DAT_11de9a44 (DAT_11de9a44 = 0.001f, ms->sec) -> local_8

gate: if (*(param_1+0x24) >= 0) && ( *(param_1+0x24) > 0 || *(param_1+0x20) != 0 ) && (local_c < local_8): transition considered too-soon-cached; if local_8 <= DAT_11de9918 return 1(accept) else { *(param_1+0x70) += 1 (violation counter); return 0(reject) }
else store last-sync time: *(param_1+0x20)=param_5, *(param_1+0x24)=param_6; return 1
param_1+0x20/0x24 = last sync time (I64d pair), param_1+0x70 = reject count, param_1+0x74 = attempt count
functions.serverRelevance: validation (authoritative timing/legality gate against skill-state spoofing; DAT_11de9a44=0.001 ms scale, DAT_11de9918 is a floor threshold)
functions.notes: Strings: 'Request to goto unkown state', 'Skill not match state or has no transition', 'currenst state ... takes %.2f and limited %.2f', 'Last sync time = %I64d, current = %I64d, multiplier = %.3f'. Names via FUN_10f57110 (GetModelString/name). This is the money function for reproducing server-side skill-transition rate limiting.

functions.purpose: Parses a 'Sequence' XML/config node into a runtime skill animation-sequence object. Reads boolean flags into a packed bitfield at param_1+0x116/0x117, an int Layer (0x114), SkillID (0x80), and iterates child event lists (AnimationNode, SoundEvent, EffectEvent, PhysicEvent, TriggerEvent, AttachmentEvent, SkillEvent, SkillRotateEvent, NextSequences) building per-event objects. Sorts SkillRotateEvent list by a float key (+4) using an introsort/insertion-sort hybrid.
formulas: flags packed into *(param_1+0x116): DisablePhy -> bit3 (val<<3 &0x08), DisableColWithWall -> bit4 (<<4 &0x10), IsLoop -> bit6 (<<6 &0x40), CatchUpDist(present) -> bit5 (<<5 &0x20)
*(param_1+0x117): EnableMoveSplineScale -> bit2 (<<2 &0x04)
Layer: *(byte*)(param_1+0x114) = (byte)Layer
SkillID read into param_1+0x80 (getter vtbl+0x74)
SkillRotateEvent sort: heap-depth = floor(log2(count)) computed via loop; FUN_11069c20 (introsort) then FUN_11069b80 (final) with threshold 0x10; insertion sort compares *(float*)(evt+4)

timer handle at param_1+0x5f (-1 = none)

activate -> owner.vtbl+0x10(this, 1); deactivate -> owner.vtbl+0x10(this, 0)

functions.purpose: Arms a buff's duration/expiry timer (param_2 = duration in ms). If the buff is server-controlled (buffInfo+0x420 != 0), it just records expiry wall-clock and server-tick without scheduling a local timer. Otherwise (client-owned, timer slot +0x24 == -1) it schedules a periodic scheduler tick, accounting for the tick granularity (1000/tickRate).

wall expiry: *(DWORD*)(param_1+0x1c) = GetTickCount() + duration; server-tick expiry: *(param_1+0x20) = duration/1000 + serverTick(iVar2)
server-buff path (*(bufObj+0x420)!=0): set +0x1c and +0x20 as above, return (no local timer)

client path (+0x24 == -1): tickRate = vtbl+8(); step = 1000/tickRate; timerArg = step + duration; schedule FUN_10a127d0('CBuffBase::_AddTimer', timerArg, 1, this, FUN_1141c470); on success store handle +0x24, and +0x1c = step + tick + duration, +0x20 = timerArg/1000 + serverTick
functions.serverRelevance: authoritative (buff duration expiry; server-controlled buffs bypass local timer). Struct: buff+0x1c = wall-clock expiry (ms), +0x20 = server-tick expiry, +0x24 = local timer handle, +0x34 = timed flag, +0x40 = buffInfo ptr, +0x44 = buff-system

if *(entry+0x4c)!=0 && !FUN_114e0340(*(entry+0x4c)) -> 0xE2

functions.purpose: XML/attr config loader for a 'LemonSkill' record. Reads sub-record at param_1+0x9c (0x24-byte stride records), then reads the wide-string attribute 'LemonSkill', tokenizes it on ';' and atoi()s each token into an int vector (the skill-id list).
formulas: Delimiter = 0x3b = ';' (passed to tokenizer FUN_100e4b30).
Per token: local_470 = atoi(token); token records stride 0x18 (24) bytes (iVar8 += 0x18).

Sub-record vector at param_1+0x9c grows by 0x24 (36) bytes per element; when *(param_1+0x9c)==*(param_1+0xa0) a new element is emplaced (FUN_11690f00) else FUN_1167a440 fills in place and advances +0x24.
int vector push: *(iVar5-8) == *(iVar5-4) -> grow (FUN_10463c40) else *piVar1=val; *(iVar5-8)+=4.
functions.serverRelevance: client-only config loader, but defines the authoritative schema: 'LemonSkill' is a ';'-separated list of skill IDs stored as an int vector.
functions.notes: vtbl calls on param_2: +0x10=HasAttr, +0x24=GetString. FUN_100f67b0 registers the attr name; DAT flag bits are one-time init guards. FUN_11a89daa=stack-cookie check.

functions.purpose: Config loader for a monster body-part record (part-break / stagger / elemental-buildup definition). Reads PartID (looks up/creates part record iVar2 via FUN_11680c60), PartName, then per-element resistance/accumulation values, Scar, and a 5-row table of per-attack-type loot/damage columns.
formulas: iVar2+0x14 = Unbalance (float, KO/stagger buildup), iVar2+0x18 = UnbalanceMulti (float, default DAT_11de9978)
iVar2+0x1c = Fall (float, topple/mount buildup), iVar2+0x20 = FallMulti (float)
iVar2+0x24 = WaterAcc (uint), iVar2+0x28 = WaterAccMulti (float)
iVar2+0x2c = FireAcc (uint), iVar2+0x30 = FireAccMulti (float)
iVar2+0x34 = ElectricAcc (uint), iVar2+0x38 = ElectricAccMulti (float)
iVar2+0x3c = DragonAcc (uint), iVar2+0x40 = DragonAccMulti (float)
iVar2+0x44 = IceAcc (uint), iVar2+0x48 = IceAccMulti (float)
iVar2+0x4c = Scar (float, wound buildup)

Column loop: 5 iterations (index 0..4, iVar3 step 0x10 until <0x50). Per row it reads string arrays LootSkillLv%d, DmgVal%d, Cut%d, Hammer%d, Shoot%d, Fire%d, Water%d, Electric%d, Dragon%d, Ice%d, ProcessLv%d (each %d = 1..5).

Row records: one at iVar2+0x58 stride 0xd*4=0x34 (52 bytes) carrying {back-ptr=iVar2, index}; one at iVar2+0x198 stride 4 (float LootSkillLv). Bitmasks built: field local_558 bit0=Cut present, bit1=Hammer; field uVar9 bits0..4 = Shoot/Fire/Water/Electric/Dragon (per-column present flags).
iVar2+4 set to 1 (record-loaded flag) at end.
functions.serverRelevance: authoritative-relevant: defines monster part-break thresholds (Unbalance/Fall/Scar), elemental status accumulation caps per part, and multipliers the server needs to compute KO/topple/wound and elemental buildup.
functions.notes: DAT_11de9978 = default multiplier constant (uninitialized in dump; likely 1.0f). Also formats 'Parts.%s.' and recurses FUN_1188e230. vtbl +0x20=GetInt, +0x2c=GetUInt(byref), +0x30=GetFloat, +0x34=GetDouble(byref).

functions.purpose: Refreshes an entity's active buff/abnormal-state display+selection. formulas: Buff-entry vector: base=*(param_1+0x42c), end=*(param_1+0x430), stride 4; each entry object has buff-info sub at *entry+0x118 and secondary at *entry+0x168; entries collected when either is nonzero (cap 100).
Priority selection scans for entry with *(buff+0xf4)==1, then ==2, then ==3 (abnormal-status priority order 1>2>3).
If a buff has *(buff+0x50)==0x3ed (1005): param_1+0x420 = *(buff+0x144).
If a buff has *(buff+0x50)==0x3ef (1007): param_1+0x428 = *(buff+0x144).
Text substitution tokens '{'=0x7b, '}'=0x7d; 4 replacement key/value pairs (local_84/local_5c/local_34/local_c) via FUN_116a71d0/FUN_10897f50.
functions.serverRelevance: mixed: abnormal-status priority ordering (fields at buff+0xf4 values 1/2/3) and buff-type ids (buff+0x50) are gameplay-authoritative concepts; the {token} string build is client HUD. Value read from buff+0x144.
functions.notes: Buff struct offsets: +0x50=type/id, +0xf4=priority class, +0x144=magnitude/value, +0x118 & +0x168=sub-info ptrs. Buff-id constants 0x3ed(1005) and 0x3ef(1007).

functions.purpose: Config loader for a skill display/definition record with associated buffs. Reads id fields, resolves skill type/category, level, group counters, name/ICON/Tips/SkillVideoID, and a decoded buff-id list; registers each buff and adds itself to a vector at +0xac.
formulas: +0x10, +0x14 = two id/int fields; +0x18 = wide-string name; type = FUN_118998f0(name) -> +0x40.
Guard: proceeds only if type != 0xd (13) and FUN_11679c30() != 0 (context/server-side flag).

+0x44 = level field, then decremented by 1: if result == -1 increments counter array &DAT_12397564[type*4], else increments &DAT_12397598[type*4] and reads +0x48, +0x4c and registers mapping (FUN_1169f290).
String name -> +0x54 area name, ICON -> +0x8c, Tips wide-string, SkillVideoID string.
buffCount = DecodeBuffIdList(SkillVideoID-string, param_1+0x54, 0xd) -> +0x50; loops registering each buff via FUN_1169ef30(buffId, *(param_1+0x10)).
Self appended to vector at param_1+0xac (grow at +0xb0).
functions.serverRelevance: mixed: ICON/Tips/Video are client UI, but the skill type classification, level, and the associated buff-id list (DecodeBuffIdList) and skill->buff registration are gameplay-relevant.

functions.purpose: Config loader for a per-level reward record: LEVEL_ID, a second field, an (ITEM_ID, ITEM_COUNT) pair pushed into a vector, and a (BUFF_ID, BUFF_COUNT) -> BUFF_ITEM_ID mapping.

If ITEM_ID>0 and ITEM_COUNT>0: push {ITEM_ID, ITEM_COUNT} (8-byte pair) into vector at param_1+0x1c (advance +8).
If BUFF_ID>0 and BUFF_COUNT>0 and BUFF_ITEM_ID>0: build key {BUFF_ID, BUFF_COUNT} (FUN_115b6a40), map-insert (FUN_104ef0a0) value = BUFF_ITEM_ID.
costs: ITEM_COUNT = item quantity granted; BUFF_COUNT = buff stack/count.
functions.serverRelevance: authoritative: defines items and buffs granted at a level; server dispenses rewards.

functions.purpose: IXmlNode config deserializer for an activity/quest 'kill monster' objective. Reads scalar fields by attribute name, stores groupId into owner+0x10, then packs the remaining 16 int fields into a fixed 0x40-byte record appended to the objective vector at owner+0x18 (end ptr owner+0x1c). Standard MHO Read pattern: vtable+0x10=HasAttr(nameId), +0x20=ReadInt(nameId); missing fields emit a client warning (FUN_100ea3b0/FUN_100ee330) and leave the slot uninitialized.
formulas: record element size = 0x40 bytes (16 int32); appended by *(owner+0x18) += 0x40 or via FUN_11a241d0 grow-and-insert when full
groupId -> *(owner+0x10)
functions.serverRelevance: config-schema (shared authoritative game data). Parsing itself is client-side, but the objective spec — targetMonsterID/targetCount, second target pair, and the MonsterBuffID1..3 applied for durations Time1..3 — must be enforced/applied by the server.
functions.notes: Fields: groupId, spawnGroupId, msgID, logic, targetMonsterID, targetCount, TargMsgID, targetMonsterID2, targetCount2, TargMsgID2, MonsterBuffID1, MonsterBuffID2, MonsterBuffID3, Time1, Time2, Time3, AlertMsgID. Once-flags cached in DAT_123a8514 (bit0=name registered per field). FUN_100f67b0 interns the attribute name.

formulas: record element size = 0x30 bytes (12 int32); *(owner+0x18) += 0x30, else FUN_11a25470 grow-insert
groupId -> *(owner+0x10)
functions.serverRelevance: config-schema (shared authoritative). Server enforces itemId/itemNum requirement and applies MonsterBuffID1..3 for Time1..3.
functions.notes: Fields: groupId, itemId, itemNum, spawnGroupId, msgID, TargMsgID, MonsterBuffID1..3, Time1..3, AlertMsgID. Once-flags in DAT_123a8670.

groupId -> *(owner+0x10)

functions.purpose: Config deserializer for a pet-skill/buff record keyed by a composite (skillId*100+level) index. Reads two int fields (owner+0x14, owner+0x18), two string fields (via ReadWString + FUN_100e5530; passed to the mislabeled CPet::SetName global-name helper), int at owner+0x24, owner+0x28, and BuffID -> owner+0x2c. Finally derives the composite key.
formulas: composite key: *(owner+0x10) = *(owner+0x14) * 100 + *(owner+0x18)  (skill/group id * 100 + level)
BuffID -> *(owner+0x2c)
functions.serverRelevance: config-schema (shared authoritative). The *100+level keying is the notable rule; server uses the same key to resolve which BuffID a pet skill grants at a given level.
functions.notes: Field names for the first 6 fields are stripped to DAT_ pointers (DAT_11d43284, DAT_11d46564, DAT_11d710fc, DAT_11d3f8a0, DAT_11d71104, DAT_11d71110); last field is literal 'BuffID'. Once-flags in DAT_123aa950. CPet::SetName call is a Ghidra mislabel of the generic string-store helper (see pet.md note).

functions.purpose: The XML/TLV deserializer for CPetSkillInfo records — the 'Read_0x99' reader that schema/docs/pet.md states was NOT present in the pet bundle and 'loaded elsewhere'. This is it. Populates the full CPetSkillInfo struct: displayId(+0x10), name (string), level(+0x18), +0x1c, +0x20, +0x24(skillGroupId), +0x28, +0xec, two 0x30-byte blocks parsed from string via FUN_10a199b0 into +0x30..0x5c and +0x60..0x8c (vec/param arrays), +0x94, a linked-id list into vectors at +0xd8 and +0xe4 (linkedSkillIds, split into two groups of 4), and a per-level 'BuffLV%d' (1..5) table of 0x10-byte entries starting at +0x98. Each parsed BuffLV id is validated against the buff manager's red-black tree (FUN_11679c30, root at +0x8d4); a missing buff triggers FUN_10c3d580(0xc) (fatal / does-not-return).
formulas: displayId -> +0x10; level -> +0x18; skillGroupId -> +0x24 (offsets match pet.md CPetSkillInfo table)
linkedSkillIds: id-list of 4-byte ints split into vector at +0xd8 (first 4) and +0xe4 (next 4); count = (list_end - list_begin) >> 2, processed only when (count & 3)==0

BuffLV table: attribute names formatted 'BuffLV%d' for d=1..5 (FUN_1167e120(L"BuffLV%d",1,5)); each entry is 0x10 bytes written sequentially from +0x98 (stride 0x10, loop bound local_480 < 0x50 = 5 entries)
buff-id validation: for each BuffLV entry with id!=0, binary-search buff manager tree at (mgr+0x8d4); abort FUN_10c3d580(0xc) if not found
functions.serverRelevance: config-schema (shared authoritative). Defines the authoritative CPetSkillInfo dataset (skill id/level/group, linked skills, per-level buff refs) that the server needs to validate pet-skill casting and apply the correct buff per skill level. Buff-existence validation here is client-side, but the same referential integrity applies server-side.
functions.notes: Resolves the open question in pet.md ('NO XML/TLV reader present in this bundle'). Field names stripped to DAT_ pointers except literals 'BuffLV%d' and '>f:yL'. FUN_10a199b0 parses a whitespace/token string into a 0x30-byte numeric block (used twice — likely min/max stat or effect-param tuples). Once-flags in DAT_123aac60. Buff manager accessor FUN_11679c30 matches the buff-system singleton. Cross-ref: pet.md CPetSkillInfo offset table (displayId 0x10, level 0x14/0x18, skillGroupId 0x24, linkedSkillIds 0x80, val_0x94).

functions.purpose: Config deserializer for a small record carrying a 'Buff' id plus id/string fields. Standard Read idiom, direct member writes (no vector).

functions.serverRelevance: config-schema (shared authoritative). Associates a Buff id with this record; server applies the referenced buff.
functions.notes: All field names except 'Buff' are stripped to DAT_ pointers (DAT_11d73d5c id, DAT_11d3ef8c/DAT_11d4cbe8/DAT_11d44360 strings, DAT_11d73d68 int). Once-flags in DAT_123ae264. Exact owning class unresolved — low confidence on record identity.

functions.purpose: Client UI marshaller that builds a PROPERTY_VO_CLASSNAME view-object describing the local player's combat stats plus the element/status flags of both weapon slots and the active armor/equipment skill list. Reads the player object (param_5, a CPlayer-like whose vtbl+0xb8 fills a scratch buffer) and pushes ~30 named fields into an AS3 data object. Guarded by param_6>1.

Weapon element/status bitmask lives at *(uint*)(weaponSlot+0x78). Per-bit booleans emitted (FUN_104d15e0): bit0,bit1,bit2 (fire/water/thunder tolerances group per string order), bit3 = weaponAttackContainsDragon, bit4 = weaponAttackContainsIce, bit6 = weaponAttackContainsPoison, bit7 = weaponAttackContainsSleep, bit8 = (11dd64fc string) e.g. paralysis. Attribute type detection: ((uint)param_5[7] & 0x8f) == 3 or == 4 selects weapon-attack container pointer param_5[8], else sentinel 0xdeadbeaf.

Armor/equipment skill iteration (two lists at playerRec+0x48 loop): base = *(int*)(rec+0x48), count = (*(rec+0x4c) - base)/0x14 (stride 0x14=20 bytes). Per non-null entry emits skillName=*(entry+0x18), needPoint=*(entry+0x24), skillEffect=(entry+0x1c), bIsActivation=1, bCanBeLighten=*(byte)(entry+8). Same pattern repeated for a second list (activated vs available skills).

A third skill list built under piStack_84[0x9838] non-zero: 10-iteration table (iVar5=10) stepping puVar6 += 0x12 words per row, emitting a 'collumn' grid; used when player has some feature flag at CPlayer+0x9838*4.
Emits floats via FUN_104d14d0 (setFloat, e.g. luckattack) and CPlayer::GetHuntRankOrCount() for hunt-rank/hrLevel fields.
curendure/endure flag: ((byte)uStack_d4 & 0x8f) == 10 (AS3 string-type discriminant).

functions.purpose: Client UI builder for the farm/garden panel: builds a CP_VO_CLASSNAME list of 'collect pets' (0x98 entries) and a PLANT_VO_CLASSNAME list of 3 plant plots, computing collectability and remaining time from server timestamps. Uses _time64 for now.

maxLevel = *(int*)(FUN_117c7e70() + petTypeOffset).

canCollect logic: _Var11 = _time64(0); now = (int)_Var11. If ( *(short*)((int)piVar9+2)==0 && piVar9[1]!=0 && ((uint)(now - piVar9[1]))/0x3c < *(uint*)(cfg+0x1c) ) then canCollect=0 else 1. (0x3c=60, converts seconds to minutes; cfg+0x1c = required minutes.)
totalTime = (piVar9[1] + *(int*)(cfg+0x1c) * 0x3c) - now   (start-timestamp + requiredMinutes*60 - now = seconds remaining).
If cfg (FUN_108e1450 result) is null: canCollect emitted with no value (default) and totalTime=0.

Plant loop: 3 plots (iVar3<3), record piVar7 advances +3 ints. seedID via FUN_10254130; state=*(piVar7+2). totalTime = FUN_114219c0(0,iVar3) (server remaining time). canCollect = (iVar6!=0 && iVar8<=0) ? 1 : 0 where iVar8 = totalTime.
petSkillList emitted as nested list per collect-pet (FUN_11a98a70 array + setter vtbl+0x14).
costs: cfg+0x1c = required grow/produce minutes per collect-pet type (time gate, not currency).
functions.serverRelevance: client-only display; server is authoritative for the collect timestamps (piVar9[1] start time), required-minutes config (cfg+0x1c), and plant remaining time (FUN_114219c0). Server must validate canCollect (elapsed>=required) before granting the collect reward. Confirms fields: level, maxLevel, canCollect, totalTime(seconds), seedID, state, itemIconPathName.

functions.purpose: Registers the player's full action-name table via FUN_1083ab70(name,len): movement/combat verbs (holster, interact, defense, reload, dodge, crouch, creep) plus rage_1/rage_2/rage_3/rage_transmission and the full xi_switch_* gamepad button set. Initializes 0x25(37) history/binding slots (copying default DAT_11cc06d8), then iterates 0x24(36) action-string entries binding each via FUN_10f40c80. Finally re-binds 3 rage action-map handlers (offsets 0x3b0/0x3b4/0x3b8) via FUN_10f3c450/FUN_10f3bbc0.
formulas: slot init: puVar3 walks param_1+0x250, count 0x25 (37); each writes DAT_11cc06d8 at [-0x4a],[-0x25],[0]
action loop: 0x24 (36) iterations over string array at param_1+0x380 (local_c), binding via FUN_10f40c80
rage handlers: for slot in {0x3b0,0x3b4,0x3b8}: h=FUN_10f3c450(param+slot); if(h && byte@(h+0xde)==0) FUN_10f3bbc0(param+slot, *(h+0xc))
clear param_1+0x8fc = 0
functions.serverRelevance: client-only (input action-map / gamepad binding setup). rage_1/2/3/rage_transmission are the rage-mode skill input verbs.
functions.notes: Confirms rage skill inputs: rage_1, rage_2, rage_3, rage_transmission. Offsets 0x3b0/0x3b4/0x3b8 = 3 rage action-map handler pointers.

functions.purpose: Loads Libs\common\RageActionMap.xml, gets the first (index 0) action node, and reads keyAction1..keyAction4 string attributes, resolving each into a key/action id via FUN_10fbfde0 and storing into local_1c/local_20/local_24/local_28. Reads an unnamed 0x11cd68d8 attribute first. Ends with FUN_10c3d580(0x14) construction of a 0x14-byte binding record.
formulas: load path literal: "Libs\\common\\RageActionMap.xml"
for each of keyAction1..4: if(node.has(name)) { node.get(name,&str); id=FUN_10fbfde0(str); store } -> local_10 holds resolved id, copied to local_20/24/28 for actions 2/3/4
record alloc size = 0x14 bytes (FUN_10c3d580(0x14))
functions.serverRelevance: client-only (rage-mode key binding load from XML)
functions.notes: Defines up-to-4 rage key actions (keyAction1..4) from RageActionMap.xml.

functions.purpose: Parses a skill-trigger/condition XML node into an object. Reads the node name (vtable+0x7c(0x11dca14c)); if it equals a first sentinel string (0x11cfb1a4) sets type field param_1+0x24 = 1, else if it equals a second (0x11ccdb2c) sets param_1+0x24 = 3. Then reads attribute "tpeOnly" into param_1+0x2c (bool) and "skillID" into param_1+0x28 (int).
formulas: type: if(nodeName==str@0x11cfb1a4) param_1[0x24]=1 else if(nodeName==str@0x11ccdb2c) param_1[0x24]=3
param_1+0x2c = attr 'tpeOnly' (bool via vtable+0x50)
param_1+0x28 = attr 'skillID' (int via vtable+0x74)
functions.serverRelevance: validation/data: parses a skill trigger record (skillID + tpeOnly flag + type 1/3) from client data files. skillID is authoritative content; the trigger structure gates skill activation. Server should mirror the skillID<->trigger mapping.
functions.notes: Offsets on trigger obj: +0x24 type(1 or 3), +0x28 skillID, +0x2c tpeOnly (third-person-execution-only flag). tpeOnly = 'TpeOnly'.

functions.purpose: Parses an animation note-track / event string (from param_2+0xc). sscanf splits it into first token (keyword) and remaining value. Dispatches on keyword: EFFECT -> spawn effect at "Bip01 Spine" bone (via char proxy +0x1e8, scale 0x3f800000=1.0); SKILLEFFECT -> spawn skill effect on the local player (checks +0x228 local-player flag); ANIMSPEED -> set animation playback speed = atof(value)*DAT_11de9a30 via FUN_10fd9120; OnLeave -> reset anim speed to 100 (if current !=100).
formulas: token split: sscanf(str,"%[^ ]",keyword); sscanf(str,"%*s%s",value)
EFFECT: charProxy.vtable+0x1e8( value, "Bip01 Spine", &pos{0,0,0}, &rot{0,0,0}, 0x3f800000, 1,1,1,0,0 )  [scale=1.0f]
ANIMSPEED: speed = (float)atof(value) * DAT_11de9a30; FUN_10fd9120((int)speed)  [DAT_11de9a30 ~= 100.0f, so 'ANIMSPEED 1.5' -> 150]
OnLeave: if(FUN_10fd9110()!=100) FUN_10fd9120(100)  (restore default speed 100)
functions.serverRelevance: client-only (animation note-track effect spawn + playback speed). ANIMSPEED scale factor DAT_11de9a30 (~100) means stored speed is percentage*? — anim playback is visual only; server uses its own animation-duration timing.
functions.notes: Note-track keywords: EFFECT, SKILLEFFECT, ANIMSPEED, OnLeave. Base anim speed unit = 100. DAT_11de9a30 ~= 100.0f.

functions.purpose: Builds the animation state-transition graph for the current weapon class (read from actor+0x15b4). Case weapon==4: registers RageRushLow transition (PLLocomotion->RageRushLow via COMBAT_PL04_RAGERUSH_START) with callback FUN_10f73a40. Case weapon==5 (bowgun/gun): registers NoBullet (COMBAT_PL05_NOBULLET), ChangeBullet (COMBAT_PL05_CHANGEBULLET), and RageAim (COMBAT_PL05_RAGE_PRESHOOT) transitions between PLLocomotion/PLCombat/PLCharging animsets. Registers per-frame callback FUN_10f74a60.
formulas: weaponType = *(actor+0x15b4); if==0 return
state-array index: (weaponType+0x2f)*0xc byte offset into param_1 (per-weapon transition table slot)
case 4 -> RageRush transition; case 5 -> NoBullet/ChangeBullet/RageAim(preshoot) transitions
functions.serverRelevance: client-only (animation FSM/transition graph). weaponType@0x15b4 and the COMBAT_PL04/PL05 anim-state names are visual; rage-aim preshoot is client presentation.
functions.notes: actor+0x15b4 = weapon class/state id (recurs in f7a080, fbb060 skill-state code). Weapon 5 = ranged (bullet/rage-aim). Slot stride (type+0x2f)*0xc.

functions.purpose: Rage/melee input handler (gated by state short@(param_1+0x1ac)==1). param_3==2 (release/move): on any move action (moveforward/back/left/right) with nonzero velocity, zeroes velocity vector (0x154/0x158/0x15c) and issues an input command (local_2d8=0x800000). param_3==1 (press): depending on input scheme DAT_120286b8+0x9d4 (0=KB: melee1 or rage_1; 1=xi_switch_y; 2=xi_switch_y; 3=xi_switch_rb; 4=xi_thumbr_down / else xi_switch_lt combo) triggers rage/melee: builds and sends a 0x404 network packet (skill activation) via server-object vtable+0x254, or fires the combo-buffered action (state 0x234=2).
formulas: gate: short@(param_1+0x1ac)==1 else exit
input scheme = *(DAT_120286b8+0x9d4): 0=keyboard(melee1/rage_1); 1=pad(xi_switch_y); 2=pad(xi_switch_y); 3=pad(xi_switch_rb); 4=pad(xi_thumbr_down); fallback combo key xi_switch_lt
velocity offsets zeroed: param_1+0x154, +0x158, +0x15c (abs>0 test via &DAT_11de9c70 = 0x7fffffff abs mask)

rage skill send: if(actor+0x100 && FUN_10f19240() skillMgr && skillMgr.vtable[0x10]+0x1c(0x4c4b456)!=0){ build pkt: *local_8=0x404; local_8[8]=FUN_1141bd30(); local_8[10]=*(skill+8); send via (player+0x3c).vtable+0x254(pkt) }
combo path: if(byte@(param_1+0x238)==1){ func_0x12402b6c(2,1,0); param_1[0x234]=2; byte@(param_1+0x238)=0 }
functions.serverRelevance: authoritative-request: builds and sends the 0x404 skill/rage activation packet to the server (opcode field via FUN_1141bd30, skill id from skill+8). The client issues the request; server must validate skill availability, rage energy, cooldown. Movement-cancel and combo-buffer are client-local.
functions.notes: Packet opcode 0x404 = rage/melee skill activation. 0x4c4b456 = magic skill-query key. Input scheme selector at DAT_120286b8+0x9d4. State offsets: 0x1ac(active), 0x234(action state), 0x238(combo-buffered flag).

functions.purpose: Second variant of the weapon anim-transition setup (weaponType@0x15b4, valid range 1..0xc). Case weapon==1: registers UnholsteredIdle transition via COMBAT_UNHOLSTER with callback FUN_10f6b660. Case weapon==5: registers the same NoBullet/ChangeBullet/RageAim(preshoot) ranged transitions as f781b0 but with callback wrapper FUN_10fb6bf0. Registers per-frame callback FUN_10f74a60.
formulas: weaponType = *(actor+0x15b4); valid iff (weaponType-1) unsigned <= 0xb (1..12)
state slot: index = weaponType*3 + 0x8c; byte offset = index*4 into param_1
case 1 -> COMBAT_UNHOLSTER; case 5 -> COMBAT_PL05 NoBullet/ChangeBullet/RagePreshoot
functions.serverRelevance: client-only (animation FSM setup, alternate entry path)
functions.notes: Slot stride here = weaponType*3+0x8c (vs (type+0x2f)*0xc in f781b0 — same table, different addressing). Weapon range 1..12.

functions.purpose: Enter-handler for the weapon charge state. Pushes event 0x26 onto an event queue; resolves state COMBAT_CHARGE and INVALID_STATE; stores the buff name "PlayerChargeBuff" into a string field at param_1+0x85 (the buff applied while charging). Registers state callbacks FUN_10f9aa60 (param_1+0x2c list) and FUN_10f9aea0 (param_1+0x32 list); iterates/reinitializes a 0x80-stride sub-object array (param_1[0x81]..[0x82]). Sets byte@(param_1+0x86)=1 (charge active).
formulas: event pushed: 0x26
buff name string 'PlayerChargeBuff' stored at param_1+0x85 (word field 0x6b zeroed too)
sub-object array stride 0x80 bytes between param_1[0x81] and param_1[0x82]
byte@(param_1+0x86) = 1 (charging flag)
functions.serverRelevance: client-only state entry, but 'PlayerChargeBuff' is a named buff granted during weapon charge — the buff itself (duration/magnitude) is authoritative server data.
functions.notes: Charge state applies buff 'PlayerChargeBuff'. States COMBAT_CHARGE / INVALID_STATE. Event id 0x26.

functions.purpose: Scans the child nodes of an XML element (vtable+0xa0 count, +0xa8 get) for a node named "BoostBuffID"; when found reads its value attribute (attr key @0x11de661c) into param_1+0x224 and returns true. Returns false if no BoostBuffID present.
formulas: for i in 0..childCount: if(child.name=="BoostBuffID" && child.has(attr@0x11de661c)) { child.get(attr, param_1+0x224); return 1 }
functions.serverRelevance: validation/data: 'BoostBuffID' is authoritative content (the buff id granted/boosted by this skill state); parsed here into param_1+0x224 for client use. Server must own the skill->BoostBuffID mapping.
functions.notes: param_1+0x224 = boost buff id. Element name 'BoostBuffID'.

functions.purpose: Enter-handler for the charge-fall state. Pushes event 0x12; clears aim state short@(param_1+0x1ac); stores buff name "PlayerChargeBuff" into param_1+0x200 and copies byte@(param_1+0x1af) into +0x204. Registers callbacks FUN_10f9b620 / FUN_10f9b1e0, plus tick handler FUN_10f5bd40(6, FUN_10f9b100). Builds fall anim transition PLLocomotion:StartFall -> PLCharging -> NORMAL_FALL.
formulas: event pushed: 0x12
buff 'PlayerChargeBuff' -> param_1+0x200; byte@(param_1+0x204) = byte@(param_1+0x1af)
tick registration: FUN_10f5bd40(6, FUN_10f9b100)  (6 = tick group/priority)
clear param_1+0x20c = 0
functions.serverRelevance: client-only state entry; carries 'PlayerChargeBuff' (authoritative buff data) into the fall-while-charging state.
functions.notes: Charge-fall state keeps 'PlayerChargeBuff'. Event 0x12. Anim NORMAL_FALL.

functions.purpose: Initializes 3 rage-passive-ability slots (loop i=0..2) from an id array param_2. For each slot (struct base param_1+0x1e8, stride 4 dwords = 0x10 bytes): stores the ability id at [+0x18/word6]; resolves the ability object; if its state (vtable+0xa8)==0, verifies particle asset "Energy_Ability_PC.PRJ.RagePassPRJ" exists, spawns it and stores the effect handle at slot[0], and sets slot[+0xc]=0x3f800000 (1.0f intensity/scale).
formulas: loop 3 iterations (3 rage-passive slots); slot stride = 4 dwords (0x10 bytes) starting param_1+0x1e8
slot[6] = param_2[i] (ability id)
gate: abilityObj = buffMgr(+0x7c)(id); if(abilityObj && abilityObj.vtable+0xa8()==0)
if particle 'Energy_Ability_PC.PRJ.RagePassPRJ' exists: slot[0] = spawned effect; slot[3] = 0x3f800000 (=1.0f)
functions.serverRelevance: client-only (rage passive ability visual/particle). Confirms up to 3 rage-passive ability slots per player; ability ids are authoritative but effect spawn is client.
functions.notes: 3 rage-passive slots. Particle 'Energy_Ability_PC.PRJ.RagePassPRJ'. slot[3]=1.0f scale (0x3f800000).

functions.purpose: Enter-handler for the rage-transmission (rage transfer) state. Registers state RAGE_TRANSMISSION, sub-state RageTransmission with callback (local_c) and tick callback FUN_10fac4b0; sets default-next-state NORMAL_IDLE; marks byte@(param_1+0x70)=1. Builds idle anim transitions PLLocomotion:HolsteredIdle -> PLBaseAction -> NORMAL_IDLE.
formulas: state name RAGE_TRANSMISSION; sub RageTransmission; default next NORMAL_IDLE
byte@(param_1+0x70) = 1
functions.serverRelevance: client-only anim/state entry for rage transmission (transferring rage to allies). The rage-transfer mechanic itself (amount, targets) is authoritative server-side.
functions.notes: Rage transmission = rage-sharing skill. States RAGE_TRANSMISSION / RageTransmission.

functions.purpose: Shows or hides the rage/bow weapon attachment set. On entry (param_1!=0, and FUN_10fdbb90 true): re-shows the weapon_item_attachment slot (sub-object +0x44(1)). When param_2==10: hides the weapon and detaches weapon_item_attachment plus (if present) melee_arrow_item / melee_arrow_secrect / bow_rage01_A / bow_rage01_B, storing the base attachment id at param_1[0x8a3].
formulas: entry: (*param_1+0x790)() [get weapon]; if(FUN_10fdbb90()) show weapon_item_attachment (attach.vtable+0x44(1))

param_2==10: hide weapon (FUN_10fdbbf0); param_1[0x8a3] = weapon_item_attachment id; detach each of {weapon_item_attachment, melee_arrow_item, melee_arrow_secrect, bow_rage01_A, bow_rage01_B} that exists
functions.serverRelevance: client-only (weapon attachment / rage-bow visual toggle)
functions.notes: param_2==10 = a specific weapon/rage state id triggering attachment cleanup. bow_rage01_A/B are rage-mode bow visual attachments.

functions.purpose: State-machine factory: given an XML node it verifies the node is named "State", reads a required attr (@0x11dbac80, likely 'name'), and looks up an existing state by name (FUN_10fde580). If absent, resolves the state "class" attribute (or inherits via "parent") and allocates the concrete state object whose byte-size is chosen per class name (giant if-chain: Charge=0x220, NormalCombo/InteractEmotion/GunAction/WE05Rage01Shoot=0x200, HolsteredIdle=0x2d0, HolsteredRun=0x2d8, UnholsteredIdle/UseItem/SharpenWeapon/WE05Rage01Reload/Aim=0x1f0, UnholsteredRun/DefenseSuccess/DefenseFailed=0x1f8, Defense=0x1e0, Standard/CollectRestart/Injury/PLInjuryLevelN=0x1e8, Dodge/SlashAxeDodge=0x208, ChargingIdle=0x218, ChargingRun/ChargingSpinAttack=0x220, Abnormal=0x1d8, InjuryFly/PLInjuryLevel11-12=0x258, InjuryRun=0x250, Lance/GunLance rage/SlashAxe holster=0x230, PLStateFly=0x240...). Then dispatches its child sections: Basics->FUN_10fb9dd0, Extend->FUN_10fba900, Transitions->FUN_10fbab00, DefenseSuperArmor->FUN_10fbaba0.
formulas: must be node 'State' with attr@0x11dbac80; else *param_2=0

class->object size map (operator new size via FUN_10c3d580): Charge 0x220; NormalCombo 0x200; InteractEmotion 0x200; HolsteredIdle 0x2d0; HolsteredRun 0x2d8; UnholsteredIdle 0x1f0; UnholsteredRun 0x1f8; Defense 0x1e0; DefenseSuccess 0x1f8; DefenseFailed 0x1f8; Standard 0x1e8; CollectRestart 0x1e8; Dodge 0x208; UseItem 0x1f0; ChargingIdle 0x218; ChargingRun 0x220; ChargingSpinAttack 0x220; GunAction 0x200; WE05Reload 0x218; WE05ReloadPerfect 0x218; WE05Rage01Reload 0x1f0; WE05Rage01Aim 0x1f0; WE05Rage01Shoot 0x200; WE09GunLanceRageAim 0x230; Abnormal 0x1d8; Injury 0x1e8; InjuryFly 0x258(600); InjuryRun 0x250; SharpenWeapon 0x1f0; LanceRage02_charge 0x230; SlashAxeDodge 0x208; SlashAxeSwordRunningHolster 0x230; PLInjuryLevel1..8 Front/Back 0x1e8; PLInjuryLevel11-12 Front/Back 0x258(600); PLStateFly 0x240
child section dispatch by name: Basics/Extend/Transitions/DefenseSuperArmor
functions.serverRelevance: client-only (animation/combat state-machine construction from XML). Enumerates the full player state vocabulary (combat, charge, defense, dodge, injury tiers, weapon rage states) — useful reference for the server's action/state enum, but the object sizes are client memory layout only.
functions.notes: Comprehensive state-name list: charge/normalcombo/defense/dodge/injury L1-12/abnormal/weapon-specific rage states. 'Abnormal' state = abnormal-status animation. attr@0x11dbac80 is the common 'name'/'value' key used throughout this parser cluster.

functions.purpose: Parses a state's <Basics> section. Handles child elements: EndAnims/EndAnim (appends end-anim ids to list param_1+0x19), Extensions/Extension (extension state ids -> list param_1+0x53), Callbacks (installs FUN_10fbec40), Property with sub-keys: Skill (param_1[0x71]=atoi(skillID); registers via FUN_10f19240/FUN_11398240), NoEndLastStateSkills/NoEndLastStateSkill (FUN_10f5ca90 per id), CanRotation (bool -> byte@(param_1+3)), Speed (param_1[0x75]=FUN_113b3380(value)), StateType/Component/SpecialSelectAnim (via value attr), NextHolsterStateName.
formulas: Skill: param_1[0x71] = atoi(value); FUN_10f19240(id,0xffffffff); FUN_11398240()  (binds state to a skill id)
Speed: param_1[0x75] = FUN_113b3380(value)  (parsed playback/action speed)
CanRotation: byte@(param_1+3) = FUN_10a675d0(value, str@0x11d9e058)  (compares to a bool literal)
EndAnim list appended at param_1[0x19]/[0x1a]; Extension id list at param_1[0x53]/[0x54]
functions.serverRelevance: validation/data: the state<->Skill binding (param_1[0x71] = skillID) and NoEndLastStateSkill exceptions are gameplay content; parsed client-side. Server must know which skill each action state corresponds to and skill cancel/chaining rules. Speed and CanRotation are client anim/movement.
functions.notes: Key gameplay field: state.skillID at offset 0x71. NoEndLastStateSkill = skills that don't terminate the previous state (combo chaining). offset 3 = CanRotation, 0x75 = Speed.

functions.purpose: Parses the "DefaultNextState" element of a state. Reads its value attr (@0x11dbac80); depending on the state name it names, stores the default-next-state into one of several slots: Charge/LanceRage02_charge -> generic slot (local_14 via FUN_10a72410), ChargingIdle->local_8, ChargingRun->local_c, ChargingSpinAttack->local_10, and NormalCombo/GunAction/WE05Reload/InteractEmotion/Dodge/SlashAxeDodge -> registered via FUN_1083ac30 or FUN_10f57080.
formulas: element 'DefaultNextState', value attr @0x11dbac80
branch by value name: Charge/LanceRage02_charge/ChargingIdle/ChargingRun/ChargingSpinAttack/NormalCombo/GunAction/WE05Reload/InteractEmotion/Dodge/SlashAxeDodge -> distinct storage slots
functions.serverRelevance: client-only (default anim transition target). Combo/charge default-next-state is presentation; server tracks its own action sequencing.
functions.notes: Default post-state transition table. Charge-family and combo states get dedicated slots.

functions.purpose: Parses a <Transition> node of the combat state machine. Reads: skillID (atoi; validates the skill is owned/usable via FUN_10f19240 + skill.vtable+0x58 and FUN_116cd660/FUN_116cdb80 — if the skill exists but is not usable the transition is rejected and the function returns 0); stateName (target state); rotType (camera=1 / normal=2 / default=3 stored at trans+0xc) with rotLimit (atoi -> trans+0x10); TransNoCheckHolster (bool -> trans+0x1c); c2Process (bool -> trans+0x1d); windowName (dodge=1 / combo=2 / immedodge=3 -> trans+0x18); Conditions list; OnTransitionCallbacks/OnTransition/function dispatch to a large set of transition-action handlers (HolsterItem, SetValue, SetFpsMode, FUN_10fc42c0..FUN_10fcfb20 chain); AGInputs/AGInput (action-graph input bindings).
formulas: skillID = atoi(value); validation: if(actor+0x100 && actor.+0x228 (is-local) && (skillMgr=FUN_10f19240())!=0 && skillID>0 && skillMgr.(+0x14).vtable+0x58()=='\0') { FUN_116cd660(); if(FUN_116cdb80()=='\0') return 0 }  -> transition blocked when skill not usable
on valid skillID: transitionObj(+0x14) = skillID (via FUN_10f59500 target)
rotType: camera->1, normal->2, default->3 stored at trans+0xc; rotLimit atoi -> trans+0x10
windowName: dodge->trans+0x18=1, combo->=2, immedodge->=3 (cancel-window classification)
TransNoCheckHolster -> byte trans+0x1c; c2Process(false) -> byte trans+0x1d
functions.serverRelevance: validation: this is the client-side skill-usability gate for state transitions (skillID must be owned and not locked/cooldown before the transition/skill fires; rejects with return 0 otherwise). Authoritative enforcement of skill ownership, cooldown, and cancel-window (dodge/combo/immedodge) timing must live server-side; this parser defines the data (skillID per transition, cancel-window type, rotation limits) the server needs to mirror.
functions.notes: Transition obj offsets: +0xc rotType(1 camera/2 normal/3 default), +0x10 rotLimit, +0x14 skillID, +0x18 windowType(1 dodge/2 combo/3 immedodge), +0x1c TransNoCheckHolster, +0x1d c2Process. 'immedodge'/'dodge'/'combo' = cancel windows. OnTransition handler chain FUN_10fc42c0..10fcfb20 are the ~25 transition-action opcodes (SetValue/SetFpsMode/HolsterItem + others).

functions.purpose: Iterates a named callback table ('Callbacks') read from the weapon/skill state definition (CInfoRecord::GetModelString) and dispatches each entry by name to a concrete handler. Outer key must be 'Callbacks'; then for each child it reads the child's name and, when it has a value, string-matches SetValue/SetGValue/HolsterItem/SetAGInput and a long chain of FUN_10a675d0(...) probes to ~30 weapon-effect handlers (FUN_10fc3b60..FUN_10fd0280 range). Also handles per-callback sub-keys OnEnter/Update/OnLeave/SetCanDodge/SetCannotDodge/CheckFps by pushing thunk closures (FUN_10f7ef40/FUN_10f7eff0/FUN_10f7f040/FUN_10f7f100) into the state's callback vectors at param_2+0xbc/0xc0. Ref-counted string plumbing (FUN_10c3d780/FUN_10c3dab0/DAT_123be268) throughout.
formulas: Outer table name must equal 'Callbacks' (strcmp) else whole function no-ops
child count = (**(param_1+0xa0))(); loop child = (**(param_1+0xa8))()
HolsterItem branch caches local_30 = *(param_2+0x50) before FUN_10f57110
SetCanDodge (in OnEnter/Update): pushes closure FUN_10f7ef40 into vector param_2+0xbc (grow-by-8 when +0xbc==+0xc0)
*(int*)(param_2+0xbc) += 8 on push
string heap-alloc: DAT_123be268 += _Size + 0xd on alloc, -= (*(p-4)+0xd) on free (CryString COW refcount at p-0xc, p-4=capacity)
functions.serverRelevance: client-only - drives client-side weapon animation/FX callback registration from state-machine data (SetValue/PlayWeaponFX/ShowReloading/ToggleAimMode/SetDefence etc.). No authoritative game state; server does not need this dispatch. The callback NAMES are a useful inventory of weapon FSM hooks.
functions.notes: Handler names visible in strings: SetValue, SetGValue, HolsterItem, SetAGInput, ShowReloading, SetFpsMode, WE05SetFpsMode, TerrainFX, SetRotation, PlayWeaponFX, CallCrosshairsUI, SetDefence, RotateByInput, ToggleAimMode, PlayWeaponAnim, ShowWeaponItem, SendLogicEvent, NeedResetDirByPreState. The 30-deep FUN_10a675d0 chain maps each remaining name to one handler; exact name->handler pairing not resolvable without the string table for FUN_10a675d0 args.

functions.purpose: Maps a player action/input command name (string) to an integer action-ID enum written to *param_2, returning 1 on match / 0 on no-match.
